78:1: God the Almighty says: What are these polytheists among the Quraysh asking about, O Muhammad? This was said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because the Quraysh, as has been mentioned, began to dispute and argue about what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had called them to, namely, acknowledging his prophethood, believing in what he brought from God, and having faith in the resurrection. So God said to His Prophet: What are these people asking about and arguing about? The words in and about in this context have the same meaning. Mention of who said what I mentioned: Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Juhada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they began to ask each other questions, so God revealed: About what are they asking each other? * About the great report. Meaning the great report. Abu Jaafar said: God did not inform His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what they were asking about the great report: meaning: about the great report. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the great report. Some of them said: It refers to the Qur’an. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, About the great report, he said: The Qur’an. Others said: It means resurrection. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, About the great report, which is the resurrection after death. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, On the great report. He said: The great report is the resurrection after death. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, About what are they asking one another? * About the great report * About which they differ, he said: The Day of Resurrection. He said: They said: This is the day on which you claim that we live and our fathers did. He said: So they differ about it, they do not believe in it. So God said: Rather, it is a great report from which you are turning away. On the Day of Resurrection they will not believe in it. Some of the Arab scholars used to say: The meaning of this is what the Quraysh were talking about in the Qur’an. Then he changed it so that it became ‘amma as if it had the meaning of: Why are they asking about the Qur’an? Then he informed and said, in which they differ, between those who believe and those who deny, so that is their difference. And His statement, in which they differ, God Almighty says: In which they differed, they became two groups: a group that believes in it, and a group that denies it. God Almighty says: So their questioning among themselves about the report that has this description. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the report about which they differ: the resurrection after death. So the fire became divided into two groups: those who believed and those who denied. As for death, they acknowledged it because they witnessed it, and they differed about the resurrection after death. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, about which they differ: people became two men about it: one who believes and one who disbelieves. As for death, they all acknowledged it, because they witnessed it, and they differed about the resurrection after death. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, in which they differ, he said: One who believes and one who denies.
78:2: God Almighty says: About the great report.
78:3: God Almighty says: in which they differ.
78:4: And His statement: No, God Almighty says: The matter is not as these polytheists claim, who deny that God raised them to life after their death. And He, the Most High, threatened them for this statement of theirs, saying, They will know, meaning: These disbelievers who deny God's threat to His enemies will know what God will do to them on the Day of Resurrection. Then He emphasized the threat with another repetition, saying: The matter is not as they claim, that God will not revive them after their death nor punish them for their disbelief in Him. They will know that the statement is not what they said when they meet God and reflect on the evil deeds they did. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim regarding this matter: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: No, they will know the disbelievers.
78:5: God Almighty said: Then both of them will know the believers, and that is how he used to recite it.
78:6: God Almighty says, enumerating His favors to these polytheists, His kindness to them, and their ingratitude for what He bestowed upon them, and threatening them with what He has prepared for them when they come to Him, from the types of His punishment and painful torment. He said to them: Have We not made the earth a resting place for you for you to rest on and spread out on. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: Have We not made the earth a bed? meaning a carpet.
78:7: God Almighty says: And the mountains are pegs. He says: And the mountains are pegs for the earth, lest it shake with you.
78:8: God Almighty says: And We created you in pairs, males and females, tall and short, or ugly and beautiful, like His statement: Those who did wrong and their spouses (al-Saffat 37:22), meaning by it: We made them.
78:9: God Almighty says: And We have made your sleep a place of rest. He says: And We have made your sleep a place of rest and tranquility for you, in which you calm down and rest, as if you were dead and not aware, while you are alive and your souls have not left you. The Sabbath and slumber mean stillness, and for this reason the Sabbath was called the Sabbath, because it is a day of rest and tranquility.
78:10: God Almighty says: And We made the night a covering for you. God Almighty says: And We made the night a covering for you, whose blackness covers you, and whose darkness covers you, as a garment covers its wearer, so that you may rest in it and not be able to do what you used to do during the day. From this is the poet’s saying: When they put on their night clothes, or when she set up for him from the cheeks of her ears, and it was dark What he means by his saying: they put on the night is that they entered into its blackness and covered themselves with it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qatada: And We made the night a covering. He said: A rest.
78:11: And His statement: And We have made the day for livelihood means that We have made the day a light for you so that you may spread out in it for your livelihood, and act in it for the interests of your world, and seeking the grace of God in it. And He, the Most High, made the day, since it was a reason for His servants to act in it to seek livelihood in it, a livelihood, as in the saying of the poet: And the brother of worries, when worries are present, the darkness falls and his pillow does not let him sleep So he made the pillow the one who does not sleep, and the meaning is for the owner of the pillow. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The day is for livelihood, he said: They seek in it from the bounty of God.
78:12: God Almighty says: And We built above you: and We roofed over you. He made the roof a building, as the Arabs used to call the roofs of the house, which is its sky, a building, and the sky was a roof for the earth. So He addressed them in their language, as the revelation was in their language, and He said seven strong as they were strong bonds, firmly created, with no cracks or breaks in them, and the passage of nights and days does not wear them out.
78:13: And His statement: And We made a blazing lamp, God Almighty says: And We made a lamp, meaning by lamp: the sun. And His statement: blazing lamp, means: a shining torch. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We made a blazing lamp, he said: luminous. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We made a radiant lamp, meaning: a luminous lamp. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a shining lamp, he said: shining. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A shining lamp. He said: Shining means illuminating. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: A shining lamp: He said: Its light shines.
78:14: And His statement: And We sent down from the pressed clouds. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the pressed clouds. Some of them said that it refers to the winds that press in their blowing. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We sent down from the pressed clouds, the pressed clouds are the winds. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he used to recite: And We sent down with the rain-clouds, meaning: the winds. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, from the pressed clouds, he said: the wind. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: In some readings it is And We sent down with the pressed clouds: the winds. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We sent down from the pressed clouds, he said: The pressed clouds are the winds, and he recited the statement of God, Who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds (al-Rum 30:48), to the end of the verse. Others said: Rather, it is the clouds that are milked with rain but have not yet rained, like a woman who has reached the time of her menstruation but has not yet menstruated. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, From the clouds. He said: The clouds are the clouds. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We sent down from the pressed clouds, meaning: from the clouds. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: Al-Mu’asarat means the clouds. Others said: Rather, it is the sky. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say: And We sent down from the cloudy clouds he said: from the sky. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We sent down from the cloudy clouds, he said: from the heavens. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We sent down from the cloudy clouds, he said: from the sky. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that God informed us that He sent down water from the pressed clouds, which are those that have been milked with water from the clouds. We said that this is more correct, because the statement about that is based on one of the three statements that were mentioned, and there is no water in the winds, so it descends from them, but rather it descends with them. And it would have been correct for them to be winds, if the reading had been And We sent down with the pressed clouds, so since the reading was from the pressed clouds, it is known that the meaning of that is what was described. If he thought that the preposition ba was followed in such a place by someone who said that, and if that is the case, then the most likely meaning of min is other than that, and the interpretation is based on the most likely meaning of the speech. If he said: then the sky may be permissible to be intended by it, it is said: even if that is the case, then the most likely meaning of rain falling is from the clouds and not from anything else. As for his saying, flowing water, he says: flowing water, one part following the other, like the flowing blood of a body, and that is its shedding. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, flowing water, he said: pouring. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Gushing water means pouring water from the sky. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, flowing water, he said: pouring. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: flowing water. Thajjaj means pouring water. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: Flowing water means: pouring. He said: Mahran told me, on the authority of Sufyan, flowing water. He said: Continuing. Some of them said: What is meant by thajaj is: a lot. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told me, A lot of water. He said: A lot of water. In Arabic, the word thaj is not known as a lot. Rather, thaj means continuous pouring. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The best Hajj is the one with a lot of water. What he means by thaj is pouring the blood of the sacrificial animals and sacrificial animals by slaughtering them. It is said from this: I poured his blood, so I poured it out thajjan, and the blood has poured out, so he pours it out thajjan.
78:15: God Almighty says: So that We may bring forth with the water which We send down from the presses to the earth grain. Grain is everything that is contained in the crops that are harvested, and it is the plural of grain, just as barley is the plural of sha’irah, and just as dates are the plural of date. As for plants, they are the pasture that is grazed, from grass and crops.
78:16: And his saying: And gardens of swathes, meaning: And We will bring forth with that rain gardens, which are orchards. And he said: And gardens, and the meaning is: And the fruit of gardens. So he omitted mentioning the fruit because the indication of the speech about it did not require mentioning it. And his saying: of swathes, means: intertwined and gathered together. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and gardens of entwined gardens, he said: crowded together. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And gardens intertwined, meaning: gardens intertwined with one another. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And gardens intertwined, he said: intertwined. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And gardens intertwined, he said: intertwined with one another. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And gardens intertwined, he said: Some of them intertwined with others. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, And gardens intertwined, he said: intertwined. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And gardens intertwined, he said: They are intertwined, one above the other. The Arabists differed about the singular of alifs. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its singular is laf. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Its singular is laf and lafif. He said: If you wish, alifs are a plural, and its singular is also a plural, so you say: Jannat lafa’, and Jannat laf, then the laf is pluralized as alif. Another one of them said: We have not heard of the word laffa tree of lafa, but its singular is lfa’, its plural is laff, and the plural of laff is alfaf, so it is the plural of laff. The correct thing to say about this is that al-alifāf is the plural of laf or lafif, because the people of interpretation agree that its meaning is: twisted, and lafa’ is: thick, and itilāf has nothing to do with thickness unless it is directed to it being the thickness of itilāf, in which case that would be a correct interpretation.
78:17: And His statement: The Day of Judgment is a time appointed. God Almighty says: The Day on which God will judge between His creation, taking from some of them for others, will be a time appointed for what God has fulfilled for these deniers of the Resurrection, and for those like them among creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, the Day of Judgment is a time appointed, is a day that God has made great, and on which He will judge between the first and the last according to their deeds.
78:18: And His saying: The Day the Trumpet is blown is translated as The Day the Trumpet is blown, referring to the Day of Judgment. So it is as if it was said: The Day of Judgment was the appointed time for what We promised these people, the Day the Trumpet is blown. I have explained the meaning of the Trumpet previously, and I have mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation about it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. According to us, it is a horn in which the Trumpet is blown. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Aslam, on the authority of Bishr ibn Shaghaf, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The horn is a horn. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, On the Day the Trumpet is blown, and the Trumpet means creation. His saying: And you will come in groups, means: They will come in groups, and in groups. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, In groups, he said: Groups, groups. It was said: You will come in groups because every nation to which God sent a messenger will come with the one to whom he sent it, as He said: On the Day We will call every people with their leader (al-Isra’ 17:71).
78:19: And His statement: And the heaven was opened and became doors, God Almighty says: And the heaven was split and cracked, and became paths, and before it was strong with no cracks or fissures in it. And it was said that the meaning of that is: And the evening was opened and became pieces like the cracked pieces of wood for the doors of houses and dwellings. They said that the meaning of the statement is: And the heaven was opened and became pieces like doors. So when the kaf was dropped, the doors became the predicate, as is said in the statement: Be Abdullah a lion, meaning: like a lion.
78:20: And His statement: And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage, meaning: And the mountains will be blown away and uprooted from their roots, and will become scattered dust, to the eye of the observer, like a mirage that one who sees it from a distance thinks it is water, but in reality it is dust.
78:21: God Almighty means by His statement: Hell was lying in wait for its inhabitants, who denied it in this world and the return to God in the Hereafter, and for others who believed in it. The meaning of the statement is: Hell was lying in wait for those who would pass through it and lay in wait for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Mazini, who said: When Al-Hasan recited this verse, Indeed, Hell is an ambush, he would say: Beware, there is an ambush at the door, so whoever brings permission will pass, and whoever does not bring permission will be detained. Yaqub told me, he said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Indeed, Hell is an ambush, he said: No one will enter Paradise until he passes through Hell. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, Hell is an ambush, teaches us that there is no path to Paradise until one crosses the Fire. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: Indeed, Hell is an ambush. He said: It has three bridges over it.
78:22: And His statement: For the transgressors is a place of return. God Almighty says: Hell is for those who transgressed in this world, transgressing the limits of God, out of arrogance towards their Lord. It was a home and a place of return to which they would return, and a destination in which they would reside. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: For the transgressors there is a place of refuge: meaning a home and shelter. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: Ma’aba means: a place of return and a home.
78:23: And His statement: They will abide therein for ages. God Almighty says: These tyrants in this world will abide in Hell, and will remain there for ages. The reciters differed in their recitation of his saying labithin. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, recited it labithin with an alif, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited labithin without an alif. The more eloquent of the two recitations and the more correct in pronunciation in Arabic is the recitation of the one who recited it with an alif. This is because the Arabs hardly ever make an adjective precedent if it comes with a verb, and then make it apply to something and make it accusative. They hardly ever say: This man is stingy with his money, or It is not difficult for us, or They are our opponents, because the verb does not come as an adjective except with praise or blame, so praise and blame do not apply to anything else. If they want to apply that to a noun or something else, they make it an agent: He is stingy with his money, and He is greedy for what we have. Therefore, I said: labithin is more correct in pronunciation in Arabic and more eloquent. I did not permit the recitation of the one who recited labithin, even though something else is more eloquent, because the Arabs sometimes apply praise to nouns. A verse of Labid may be recited: Or a broken bone made by a smooth muscle, its navel is covered with scars and wounds So I did a work in the support, and if it was a worker it would be more eloquent, and he also recites: And with an axe, I strike the heads of the cranes Including the saying of Abbas bin Mirdas: I am more stubborn and protective of the truth than them, and I strike with the strongest swords. As for the eras, it is the plural of era, and eras is the plural of era, as the poet said: We lived like my two friends for a long time until it was said that we would never split up. The plural of this is Haqab, and among the epochs whose plural is Haqab is God’s statement, Or I shall pass on for ages (al-Kahf 18:60). This is one of the epochs. The interpreters differed on the duration of the era. Some of them said: It was a period of three hundred years. Who said that? Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz told us, on the authority of Abdul-Warith bin Saeed, who said: Ishaq bin Suwaid told us, on the authority of Bashir bin Kaab, regarding His statement, remaining therein for ages, he said: It has reached me that an age is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years. Others said: Rather, the duration of one era is eighty years. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Ammar Al-Dahni told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said to Hilal Al-Hijri: What do you find about the periods in the revealed Book of God? He said: We find it to be eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, and each day a thousand years. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that he said: A period is eighty years, a year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is one thousand years. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The period is eighty years. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, regarding his statement, remaining therein for ages, he said: A lifetime is eighty years, a year is three hundred and sixty days, a day is a year or a thousand years. Al-Tabari is uncertain. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said, They will abide therein for ages, meaning that it is without interruption. Whenever an age passes, another age comes after it. He told us that an age is eighty years. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, eras, he said: We have been informed that an era is eighty years of the years of the Hereafter. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas: They will abide therein for ages. Only God knows the number of these ages, but one age is eighty years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, each day of which is a thousand years. Others said: One era: seventy thousand years. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told me, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Salim, who said: I heard al-Hasan being asked about the statement of God, They will abide therein for ages. He said: As for the ages, they have no number other than eternity in the Fire, but they mentioned that one age is seventy thousand years, and each day of those seventy thousand days is like a thousand years of what you count. Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, They will abide therein for ages, he said: As for the ages, no one knows what they are. As for one age: it is seventy thousand years, each day like a thousand years. It was narrated on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan regarding this verse, that it is about the people of the Qiblah. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Amer bin Jashab, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, regarding his statement, They will abide therein for ages, and his statement, except what God wills, that they are regarding the people of monotheism from the people of the Qiblah. If someone were to say: What do you say about this hadith? It would be said: What Qatada said on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas is more authentic. If we say: Then there is no punishment for the disbelievers with God except for ages, it is said: Al-Rabi’ and Qatadah said: These ages have no end or interruption. It is possible that the meaning of that is: They will remain in it for ages, in this type of punishment, which is that they will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and pus. So when those ages have ended, there will be other types of punishment for them, as God, the Most High, said in His Book: “And indeed, for the transgressors is the worst place of return: Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the resting place. So let them taste it: scalding water and pus. And other pairs like it.” (Surah Sad: 55-58) This statement, in my opinion, is more similar to the meaning of the verse. It was narrated on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan regarding this matter: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us: I asked Abu Muadh al-Khurasani about the statement of God, They will abide therein for ages, so he informed us on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, who said: It is abrogated. It was abrogated by We will not increase you except in torment (an-Naba’: 30). This statement has no meaning, because His statement, They will abide therein for ages is a report, and there is no abrogation in reports. Rather, abrogation occurs in commands and prohibitions.
78:24: And his statement: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, meaning: They will not taste therein any coolness that would suffocate them from the blazing heat, except for the boiling water, nor any drink that would quench their thirst except for the scalding water. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language have claimed that the coolness in this place is sleep, and that the meaning of the statement is: They will not taste therein any sleep or drink. And he cited as evidence for his statement that the statement of al-Kindi: Her sheets cooled on me, so the cold pushed me away from her and her kisses. By cold, he means drowsiness, and sleep cools the thirst, so it was called cold because of that, so it is not by its known name, and the interpretation of the Book of God is mostly from the well-known speech of the Arabs, and not from anything else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except scalding water and purulent water. 78:25: And His statement: Except scalding water and pus. God Almighty says: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink except scalding water that has been boiled until its heat has reached its peak, so it is like molten brass that scalds faces. And no coolness except pus. The interpreters differed about the meaning of ghassaq. Some of them said: It is the pus that flows from the people of Hell. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah ibn Sa`d, regarding His statement, Boiling water and pus-filled water, he said: It is what flows from their skins. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father: Abu Amr told us: Ikrimah claimed that he told them about His statement, and pus, that he said: What comes out of their eyes of pus and blood. Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim and Abu Razin: Except for scalding water and pus. They said: The water that washes the people of Hellfire. This is the wording of Ibn Bashar. As for Ibn Al-Muthanna, he said in his hadith: What flows from their pus. Ibn Bashar told us, once again, on the authority of Abdul Hamid, and he said as he said: Ibn Al-Muthanna. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin: And Ghasaqan means what flows from their pus. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur and Abu Razin, on the authority of Ibrahim, similarly. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Ghasaqan, we used to say that ghasaq is what flows from between his skin and flesh. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Al-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, that he said: It was reported to me that their tears did not flow. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And Ghasaqan he said: What flows from their pus from the cold. Sufyan said: And others said: Tears. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, except for scalding water and pus, he said: The scalding water is their tears in the Fire, which collects in the ditches of the Fire and they are given it to drink, and the pus is the pus that comes out of their skins, from what the Fire melts them in pools in which it collects and they are given it to drink. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: Except for boiling water and pus. He said: Pus is what drips from their skins and what flows from their stench. Others said: Ghasaq: cold. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except scalding water and pus-filled water, meaning: freezing cold. Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa’ib, and Ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, except scalding water and pus-filled water, he said: That which they cannot taste because of its coldness. He said: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, Except scalding water and pus. He said: That which they cannot bear because of its coldness. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Al-Ghasaq means that which cannot be tolerated due to its coldness. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, who said: Al-Ghasaq is the freezing cold. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, who said: Al-Ghasaq is the freezing cold. Others said: It is the stinking one, and it is in Al-Takhariyyah. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, on the authority of Salih bin Hayyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah, who said: Al-Ghasaq in Takhariyyah means the stinking one. And in my opinion, ghassaq is the active participle from their saying: Ghasaqat ‘ayn so-and-so meaning that his tears flowed, and ghassaq al-jarh means that its pus flowed, and from this is the saying of God, And from the evil of Ghasiq when it comes (al-Falaq 113:3). What is meant by ghassaq is the night when it covers and envelops things, and what is meant by that is its attack on things like the attack of a flowing torrent. So if ghassaq is what you described of the flowing thing, then it is necessary to say: What God promised these people, and informed them that they will taste in the Hereafter of drink is the liquid from the freezing cold in Hell, which is combined with its intense cold and putridness. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ya`mar bin Bishr told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us: Rashdin bin Sa`d told us: Amr bin Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a bucket of filth were to be poured into the world, the people of the world would stink. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Harb, who said: Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Qabil, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: Do you know what Ghasaq is? They said: God knows best. He said: It is thick pus. If a drop of it were to be spilled in the West, it would stink the people of the East, and if it were to be spilled in the East, it would stink the people of the West. If someone were to say: You have said that Ghasaq is freezing cold, and freezing cold is extreme cold, so how can freezing cold be a liquid? 78:26: God Almighty says: This punishment with which these infidels were punished in the Hereafter, their Lord did it to them as a recompense, meaning: as a reward for their evil deeds and words that they used to do in this world. It is a source of the saying of the speaker: This punishment matched this deed in accordance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, a just reward means: in accordance with their deeds. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, a just recompense means the recompense was in accordance with the people’s evil deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`: A just reward. He said: According to their deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`, regarding his statement, a just reward, he said, a reward that matches their deeds. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, A just recompense, he said: They did evil, so they were recompensed evil, and they did good, so they were recompensed good. Then he recited the statement of God, Then the worst was the end of those who did evil (al-Rum 30:10). Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, a just reward, he said: A reward that matches the deeds of the people. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A reward in accordance with the deed. He said: The reward is in accordance with the deed.
78:27: And His statement: Indeed, they did not expect an account. God Almighty says: Indeed, these disbelievers were in this world not afraid of God calling them to account in the Hereafter for His blessings upon them, His kindness to them, and their poor gratitude to Him for that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They do not expect an account, he said: They do not care, so they believe in the unseen. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, they did not expect an account, meaning they did not fear an account. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, they did not expect an account, he said: They did not believe in the Resurrection or the Account, and how could one expect an account when he was not certain that he would live, nor was certain of the Resurrection? And he recited the statement of God, “Rather, they said like what the former ones said. They said, ‘When we have died and become dust,’…” until His statement, Legends of the former peoples. (Surat al-Mu’minun 23:81-83), and he recited, Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, when you are torn apart, completely?… until His statement, new (Surat Saba’: 7). So some of them said to one another, What is wrong with him? Does he invent a lie against God, or is he possessed? (Surat Saba’: 8). The man is crazy when he tells us this.
78:28: And His statement: And they denied Our signs with a lie. God Almighty says: And these people denied Our arguments and proofs with a lie. It was said: With a lie, and He did not say with a lie, as a prelude to his action. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was said that because the verb from it is of four forms, so he wanted to make it like the root of af’alta and the source of af’alta is if’alan, so he said: kadhaban, so he made it according to the number of its source. He said: And on this basis you say: qātal qaṭalan. He said: And it is from the speech of the Arabs. And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: This is an eloquent Yemeni dialect. They say: khādabatu bih kadhaban, and kharak al-qamis khirāqan, and every fa’ala, its source is fa’al in their language with a shaddah. He said: An Arab once said to me on Al-Marwah, asking me: Is shaving more preferable to you than short hair? He said: And some of the Banu Kalb recited to me: You have long discouraged me from my companions and from fulfilling my need for healing. The reciters agreed to stress the dhal of kadhdhab in this place, and Al-Kisa’i in particular would stress the second, and that is in his saying: They do not hear in it idle talk nor a liar. He says: It is from their saying: I lied to him as a liar and a lie, and he stresses this one, and he says: His saying they lied restricts kadhdhab to the source.
78:29: And His statement: And everything We have recorded in a book God Almighty says: And everything We have recorded and written in books, We have written its number, its amount, and its value, so nothing of it escapes Us in knowledge. And He put book in the accusative case because in His statement We have recorded it is a source of We have established it and We have written it, as if it was said: And everything We have written in a book.
78:30: And His statement: So taste, for We will not increase you except in torment. God Almighty says: The unbelievers in Hell will be told when they drink boiling water and pus-filled water: Taste, O people, of the torment of God which you used to deny in this world. We will not increase you except in torment upon the torment you are in, neither as a lightening of it nor as a relief. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: No verse more severe than this has been revealed to the people of Hell: So taste [the [false] fruits, for We will not increase you except in punishment. He said: They will be in more punishment forever. Bishr told us, he said: Mazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment. It was mentioned to us that Abdullah bin Amr used to say: No verse was revealed to the people of Hell more severe than it: So taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment. So they will receive more from God forever.
78:31: He says: For the righteous there is a way out of the Fire and into Paradise, and a way out of it for them and a way out of it for them and a way out of what they sought. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, for the righteous is attainment. He said: They have attained success by being saved from the Fire. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment: meaning, by God, there is attainment from the Fire to Paradise, and from God’s punishment to His mercy. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Indeed, for the righteous is attainment, he said: A attainment from the Fire to Paradise. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, for the righteous is attainment, meaning: a place of refuge.
78:32: And his saying: gardens and gardens: a translation and explanation of the victory, and it is permissible to translate it from it, because the victory is a source from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so won this thing: if he sought it and won it, so it is as if it was said: the righteous will win what they sought of gardens and grapes, and gardens: the plural of garden, and it is the orchards of palm trees and grapes and trees surrounded by walls surrounding them, because the walls surround them, the garden is called a garden, so if the walls are surrounding it, he would not say garden for it, and its surrounding it: its encompassing it. His saying: And grapes means: And grape vines. He dispensed with mentioning the grapes instead of mentioning the vineyards.
78:33: And his saying: And young maidens of equal age means: And breasts of the same age. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, and full-breasted women, he said: and breasts, and his statement, of equal age, he said: of equal levels. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And young maidens of equal age, meaning: women of equal age. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And young maidens of equal age, he said: Breasts of equal age, meaning: of the same age. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, then he described what is in Paradise, he said: Gardens and grapevines * And full-breasted maidens of equal age. By that he meant women, of equal age: not of the same age. Abbas bin Muhammad told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Al-Kawa’ib: the beautiful breasts. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And young maidens of equal age, he said: Young maidens are those who have developed breasts and whose breasts are full. He said: Of equal age are of equal status, so-and-so is of equal status. He said: Of equal status are those of equal status. Nasr bin Ali told us: Yahya bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And virgins of equal age means young women.
78:34: And his saying: An overflowing cup means: And a cup that is continuously poured on its drinkers in abundance and fullness. Its origin is from dahaq which is to continuously pressure a person with force and violence. Likewise, the overflowing cup: to continuously pour it on its drinkers in abundance and fullness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Marwan told us, he said: Abu Yazid Yahya bin Maysarah told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Nastas, he said: Ibn Abbas said to his servant: Give me a drink of Dahak. He said: So the servant brought it full, and Ibn Abbas said: This is the Dahak. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Musa bin Umair told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, a full cup, he said: full. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Sulayman ibn Bilal told me, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of `Amr ibn Dinar, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked about a full cup. He said: A full cup. Yunus said, Ibn Wahb said: That which follows one another. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, a full cup, meaning: full. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding his statement, a full cup, he said: bloody. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, and a full cup, he said: full. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, A full cup, he said: The full one. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And a full cup. He said: Filled. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, a full cup, he said: brimming full. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And a full cup. He said: Full means full and replete. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, a full cup, he said: Full means overflowing. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, a full cup, he said: The full cup. Others said: Al-Dahhaq: clear. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi and Abbas ibn Muhammad told us: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Umar ibn Ata’ told us on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, And a full cup. He said: Clear. Others said: Rather, it is the successive one. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr said regarding His statement, And a full cup, “full” means continuous. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and a full cup, he said: continuous. Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And a full cup, he said: The full, continuous cup. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and a full cup, he said: successive.
78:35: And His statement: They will not hear therein any idle talk or falsehood, God Almighty says: They will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, meaning false speech, or falsehood, K says, nor falsehood, meaning they will not lie to each other. The reciters in the regions read it with a shaddah on the dhal, as I explained in His statement, And they denied Our signs falsely, except for Al-Kisa’i, who lightened it for what was described before. The shaddah is more preferable to the lightening, and the reading is with the shaddah, and I do not see the reading of that with the lightening due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters to the contrary. Among the lightening is the statement of Al-A’sha: I believed her and I disbelieved her, but a liar benefits a person. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Neither idle nor false. He said: Falsehood and sin. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, They will not hear therein any idle talk or falsehood, he said: And it is like that, there is no idle talk or falsehood in it.
78:36: It means, may He be glorified: A reward from your Lord, a gift. God gave these righteous people what is described in these verses as a reward from your Lord for their deeds, for their obedience to Him in this world. His saying, a gift, means: a favor from God to them with that reward, because He rewarded them with ten for one in some cases, and seven hundred for one in others. So this increase is a reward and a gift from God. His saying: An account means: An accounting of their deeds to God in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, A reward from your Lord, a gift of reckoning, he said: A gift from Him, an account of what they did. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: A reward from your Lord is a gift according to account. That is, a great gift. So He rewarded them for the little work with great good, which will never end. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, A gift of reckoning, he said: A great gift. Mujahid said: A gift from God as an account of their deeds. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: I heard Ibn Zayd say about the statement of God, A reward from your Lord, a gift according to account. So he recited, Indeed, for the righteous is attainment * Gardens and vineyards * And full-breasted maidens of equal age... to a gift according to account. He said: This is the reward for their deeds, the gift that He gave them. They did one thing for Him, so He rewarded them tenfold. And he recited the statement of God, Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof (Al-An`am 6:160), and he recited the statement of God, “The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain [of corn] which grows seven ears; in each ear is a hundred grains. And God multiplies for whom He wills” (Al-Baqarah 2:261). He said: He increases for whom He wills. All of this was a gift, and they were not deeds that He counted for them, so He rewarded them with it until it was as if they had worked for Him. He said: And they did not work, but rather they worked ten, so He gave them one hundred, and they worked one hundred, so He gave them one thousand. All of this is a gift, and the first work, Then He calculated that as if they had done it, so He rewarded them as He rewarded them for what they did.
78:37: And His saying: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Gracious. God Almighty says: A reward from your Lord, Lord of the seven heavens and the earth and whatever is between them of creation. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited it Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Gracious in the nominative case in both. Some of the people of Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as Lord in the accusative case and the Most Gracious in the nominative case. We have a correct interpretation of each of these, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct. However, the accusative case in Lord is more pleasing to me because of its proximity to His statement a reward from your Lord. As for the Most Gracious in the nominative case, it is better because of its distance from that. And His statement: The Most Gracious, they do not possess any power to address Him God Almighty says: The Most Gracious, none of His creation will be able to address Him on the Day of Resurrection except those among them whom He has given permission and who speak correctly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They do not possess any authority to speak to Him, he said: Speech. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, They do not possess any speech from Him, meaning any words. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They do not possess the power to address Him, he said: They do not possess the power to address God, and the one addressed is the disputant who disputes with his companion.
78:38: And his saying: On the Day the Spirit arises. The scholars differed regarding the meaning of the Spirit in this context. Some of them said: It is an angel who is among the greatest of the angels in creation. Who said that? Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told me: Rawad bin Al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The spirit is an angel in the fourth heaven. It is greater than the heavens, the mountains, and the angels. It glorifies God twelve thousand times every day. God creates from each glorification an angel from the angels. It will come on the Day of Resurrection in a row alone.” Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand, he said: He is the greatest angel in creation. Others said: It is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: On the Day the spirit rises up. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: On the Day the spirit arises. He said: The spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told us: Rawad bin Al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: On the Day the spirit rises up. He said: The spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Others said: He was created by God in the image of a prophet. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The soul was created in the image of the children of Adam, eating and drinking. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The spirit: He created for them hands and legs, and I think he said: and heads. They eat food, they are not angels. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amer told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, who said: They resemble people, but they are not people. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The soul was created like the creation of Adam. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, regarding His statement, On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, he said: The Spirit is a creation of God’s creation, and they are many times stronger than the angels. They have hands and feet. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, the freed slave of Umm Hani’, On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand. He said: The Spirit is a creation like people, but they are not people. Others said: They are the children of Adam. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, On the Day the soul rises up, he said: They are the children of Adam, and this is what Al-Hasan said. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His statement, On the Day the spirit will arise, he said: The spirit is the children of Adam. Qatada said: This is something that Ibn Abbas kept secret. Others said: It was said: These are the souls of the children of Adam. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak, he said: It means when the souls of the people will stand with the angels, between the two blasts, before the souls are returned to the bodies. Others said: It is the Qur’an. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, my father used to say: The spirit is the Qur’an, and he recited: “And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Scripture was, nor what faith was.” (al-Shura
78:39: God Almighty says: That Day means: the Day of Resurrection, which is the day of the spirit and the angels in rows. The Truth means: it is a true reality, there is no doubt about it. And His statement: So whoever wills may take to his Lord a place of return, meaning: whoever among His servants wills may take, by believing in this true Day, preparing for it, and doing what will save him from its terrors, a place of return, meaning: a return, and it is a verbal noun, from their saying: So-and-so returned from his journey, as Ubayd said: Everyone who is absent will return, but the one absent from death will not return. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So whoever wills may take a way back to his Lord. He said: They took a way back to God through obedience to Him and what brings them closer to Him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: To his Lord is a return. He said: A path. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Ma’aba means: a return home.
78:40: And His statement: Indeed, We have warned you of an imminent punishment means: Indeed, We have warned you, O people, of a punishment that has drawn near to you and is approaching. That is on the Day when a man the believer will see what his hands have put forth of good that he acquired in this world, or evil that he had done in the past, so he will hope for God’s reward for his good deeds, and fear His punishment for his bad ones. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan: On the Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth, he said: The believing man is wary of small sins and fears major sins. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Huhada, on the authority of al-Hasan: On the Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth, he said: The believing man. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Juhada, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, On the Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth, he said: The believing man. And His statement: The unbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust,’ God Almighty says: And the unbeliever will say on that day, wishing for the punishment that God has prepared for his unbelieving companions: Oh, I wish I were dust, like the animals that were made into dust. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Ibn Abi `Uday told us: Awf told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mughira, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the hide will be spread out, and the beasts, wild animals, and wild beasts will be gathered together. Then retribution will take place among the beasts, and the hornless sheep will take retribution from the horned sheep for butting it. When the retribution among the beasts is finished, He will say to them: Be dust. He said: At that time, the unbeliever will say: I wish I were dust. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar: Ja’far ibn Burqan told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: God will gather all of creation, every animal, bird, and human being, and say to the animals and birds: Become dust. Then the unbeliever will say: I wish I were dust. Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Al-Maharibi Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will judge between His creation, the jinn, mankind, and animals. And on that Day He will bind the horned ones until there is no longer any responsibility for one another. Then God will say, ‘Be dust.’ At that time the unbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust.’” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, On the Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth, the disbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust,’ while he is the doomed, the excessive, the helpless. What prevents him from saying that when the faults of his deeds have become apparent to him, and he has faced the Most Merciful while He is angry with him? So he will wish for death on that day, and there is nothing in this world more hateful to him than death. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad `Abdullah ibn Dhakwan, who said: When judgment is passed between the people and the people of Hell are ordered to be dealt with, it will be said to the believing jinn and to all the nations except the children of Adam: Return to dust. Then when the unbelievers look at them and see that they have returned to dust, the unbeliever will say: I wish I were dust. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding His statement, The unbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust,’ he said: When it is said to the animals, Be dust, the unbeliever will say, Oh, I wish I were dust.
